rules.scopeRule: One exact validated public proof or artifact authorizes at most one resource through the approved named function; caller tenant/role fields and blank scope are never authority.

Caller-provided tenant, role, purpose or routing fields are ignored or rejected as authority.
Public lists, raw protected-table queries, internal/test downloads and policy/security configuration are denied.

rules.scopeRule: An ACTIVE database-hydrated LICENSEE_ADMIN or ORG_ADMIN uses its nonblank User.licenseeId and User.orgId; a selector may only equal that scope. allowScenarios: A database-hydrated LICENSEE_ADMIN or ORG_ADMIN reads bounded risk analytics for its active licensee and organization.

An optional query licensee equal to canonical scope narrows nothing and is accepted.

The immutable RISK_ANALYTICS_READ attribution commits in the same transaction before serialization.

Blank, missing, foreign, inactive, suspended or organization-inconsistent scope is denied.
Out-of-range date/page inputs and context purpose, actor, assurance or scope mismatch are denied before analytics reads.
A protected query before context, global Prisma use, unbounded input, inconsistent tenant predicate, nested User projection or non-atomic attribution is denied.

rules.scopeRule: The exact alert and exact active incident must share one licensee and fall under one unexpired incident authorization; acknowledgement, unlinking, reassignment, and mixed-field patch requests are denied on this workflow.
allowScenarios: A database-verified active licensee administrator with fresh MFA, request ID, tenant-alert-review purpose, and canonical licensee reads at most 100 projected alerts for that licensee in one attributed transaction.
A database-verified active licensee administrator acknowledges one unacknowledged alert in their licensee through a one-row CAS and same-transaction immutable attribution.
A platform incident responder with step-up assurance and an active unexpired incident authorization reads only projected alerts bound to that incident and licensee.
An incident responder links one unlinked alert to one same-licensee incident through a one-row CAS, reason, idempotency key, immutable attribution, and approved outbox.
The identity-worker runtime delivers one allowlisted durable outbox event through worker-boundary-siem-outbox-delivery without installing human context.
denyScenarios: Generic admin, role text alone, password-only sensitive administration, missing purpose/request ID, blank or foreign scope, NULL or conflicting parents, stale assurance, or platform-wide fallback is denied.
A manufacturer cannot read all alerts for a linked licensee; no current workflow is approved for manufacturer alert details.
Assignment, PolicyAlert resolution, suppression, unacknowledgement, incident unlinking, incident reassignment, mixed acknowledgement/escalation patch, or protected ownership changes are denied.
Raw details, secret indicators, personal data, full network/device fingerprints, raw audit data, SIEM credentials, or unrelated tenant identifiers are denied.
Public access is denied; no alert ID, tenant reference, signed QR reference, or notification token currently proves a public alert disclosure.
Workers cannot impersonate humans and operators cannot replace exact procedures with direct alert-table access.

rules.scopeRule: One exact validated public proof or artifact authorizes at most one resource through the approved named function; caller tenant/role fields and blank scope are never authority.
allowScenarios: A canonical legacy code returns one minimal customer-facing verification result while the compatibility gate remains enabled.
A valid unexpired Ed25519 token bound to the stored QR, tenant, batch, nonce and epoch returns one signed result.
A valid session or support proof returns one minimal status and nothing from a foreign resource.
One-time invitation, reset and email tokens execute only their existing exact pre-auth function and consume atomically.
Feedback and intake create one bounded attributed row with server-derived routing and generic response.
A public connector request resolves one allowlisted signed artifact below the release root without database access.
denyScenarios: Blank, malformed, unknown, ambiguous, inactive, unreleased, orphaned or inconsistent scope never becomes a public wildcard.
Invalid signed tokens never fall back to raw QR lookup and unsigned claims establish no authority.
Reference, email, ticket, user, licensee, manufacturer, batch, range or internal ID alone proves nothing.
Consumed/expired tokens, stale session proofs and rotated QR epochs are denied without existence disclosure.
Caller-provided tenant, role, purpose or routing fields are ignored or rejected as authority.
Public lists, raw protected-table queries, internal/test downloads and policy/security configuration are denied.
